stem:
Which part of the sentence has an error? If the sentence is correct, choose "No error".

Every applicant need to bring two valid IDs on the day of the exam.
choices: on the day of the exam
hints: Find the subject (who does the action) and the verb (the action word). Is the subject one person or more than one?
The subject is "Every applicant". "Every" looks at people one at a time, so the subject is singular (one).
In the present tense, a singular subject takes the verb form that ends in -s: he works, she writes. Check whether the verb matches the subject, then check the other two parts.

solution.methodName: Find the true subject, then match the verb

steps.action: Find the verb: "need". Then ask who needs to bring IDs: "Every applicant". That is the subject.
steps.why: The subject is the person or thing doing the action. The applicant is the one who must bring the IDs.

steps.action: Decide if the subject is singular or plural. "Every applicant" is singular.
steps.why: "Every" and "each" point to people one at a time: this applicant, then that applicant. So treat the subject as one person, like "he" or "she".

steps.action: A singular subject in the present tense takes the -s form of the verb: "needs".
steps.why: Say it with "he": "he needs", not "he need". The same rule applies to "every applicant".

steps.action: Fix the sentence: "Every applicant needs to bring two valid IDs on the day of the exam."
steps.why: Read the fixed sentence aloud to make sure it sounds right.

steps.action: Check the other parts. "two valid IDs" is a correct plural, and "on the day of the exam" uses "on" correctly for a day.
steps.why: Always check every part before you choose. This also rules out "No error".

steps.action: The error is "need to bring". It should be "needs to bring".

trapNotes.two valid IDs: This part is correct. "Two" needs a plural noun, and "IDs" is the plural of ID. The error is in the verb, not the noun.
trapNotes.on the day of the exam: This part is correct. "On" is the right word before a day, as in "on Monday" or "on the day of the exam".
trapNotes.No error: "Need" can sound right because many applicants will come. But "every applicant" means one at a time, so the verb must be "needs".
